{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Robert Gary Bland''' (born February 25, 1948) is an American [[mathematician]] and [[operations research]]er, a professor of operations research and information engineering at [[Cornell University]].<ref name="profile">[https://www.orie.cornell.edu/people/profile.cfm?netid=rgb6 Faculty profile], Cornell University, retrieved 2012-02-25.</ref> He was born in New York City.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NCBYAAAAMAAJ&q=%22bland,+robert+gary%22|title=American men and women of science: 1989-1990 : A biographical directory of today's leaders in physical, biological and related sciences|year=1989|publisher=R.R. Bowker |isbn=9780835225694}}</ref>

Bland did both his undergraduate and graduate studies at [[Cornell University]], earning a bachelor's degree in 1969, M.S. in 1972, and a Ph.D. in 1974 under the supervision of
[[D. R. Fulkerson]].<ref name="profile"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=Robert Gary Bland|id=33940}}</ref> He began his faculty career at [[Binghamton University]], but then returned to Cornell in 1978.<ref name="profile"/>

Bland is known as one of the inventors of [[oriented matroid]]s, which he used to define [[Bland's rule]] for avoiding cycles in the [[simplex method]] for [[linear programming]].<ref>{{citation|title=Oriented Matroids|series=Encyclopedia of Mathematics and Its Applications|volume=46|first=Anders|last=Björner|publisher=Cambridge University|year=1999|isbn=978-0-521-77750-6}}. [https://books.google.com/books?id=k2an6eBxn3kC&pg=PA150 Page 150]: "It seems fair to say that the major credit for the origination of oriented matroid theory should be shared by Robert Bland, [[Jon Folkman]], [[Michel Las Vergnas]], and Jim Lawrence." This authoritative reference on oriented matroids discusses Bland's pivoting-rule on [https://books.google.com/books?id=k2an6eBxn3kC&pg=PA418 page 418].</ref><ref name="Bland">
